Problem:
A bug starts at a vertex of an equilateral triangle. On each move, it randomly selects one of the two vertices where it is not currently located, and crawls along a side of the triangle to that vertex. Given that the probability that the bug moves to its starting vertex on its tenth move is $m/n,$ where $m$ and $n$ are relatively prime positive integers, find $m + n.$


=== PLAN ===
  P1 (SETUP_EQUATION): Define the vertices of the equilateral triangle and the possible moves the bug can make.
  P2 (SETUP_EQUATION): Establish a recurrence relation for the probability of the bug being at each vertex after each move.
  P3 (COMPUTE): Use the recurrence relation to compute the probability of the bug being at the starting vertex after the tenth move.
  P4 (SIMPLIFY): Express the probability as a reduced fraction $ m/n $ where $ m $ and $ n $ are coprime.
  P5 (COMPUTE): Calculate the sum $ m + n $ for the reduced fraction.

(none)
